success_patterns: Translate each option into its hypotheses, quantifiers, and conclusion before comparing them; conjunctions, disjunctions, and changes from “some” to “every” can change the claim substantially.

Treat “strongest” as a logical comparison: select the strongest conclusion actually supported, not the most ambitious-sounding one, and verify any strengthened hypothesis or extra clause independently.
Keep distinct levels of conclusions distinct—for example, finite-time blow-up, failure of global boundedness, and global existence with unbounded norms are not interchangeable.
Check boundary and equality cases before asserting strict inequalities; a constant plateau, for instance, gives equality at its interior indices.
Preserve the stated scope of measure and uniformity, and distinguish algorithmic claims such as deciding whether a witness exists from producing the witness itself.

patch.reasoning: The successful answers depend on careful comparison of the exact logical strength of options, including quantifier scope, altered hypotheses, equality cases, and claims that are stronger than mere existence or decidability. Adding a compact comparison checklist should make this behavior reusable across theorem-grounded questions.

edits.content:
## Compare options exactly
- Rewrite each choice as **hypotheses ⇒ conclusion**, and mark the scope of every quantifier (for example, “some” versus “every,” “both” versus “at least one,” and “almost every” relative to which measure).
- Compare premises and conclusions separately. A weaker premise does not inherit an implication proved under a stronger premise; an added conclusion or algorithmic guarantee must also be justified on its own.
- Interpret extremal wording literally. Finite-time blow-up, failure of global boundedness, and global existence with unbounded norms are different claims; do not substitute one for another.
- Test equality and boundary cases before accepting strict refinements. In particular, a strict inequality cannot hold at an index where the relevant values are constant.
- Preserve the problem’s stated measure and uniform range. Do not replace a measure supported on a specified subset with ambient measure, or a bound for every parameter with one that holds only asymptotically.
- Distinguish deciding whether a witness exists from constructing the witness. Claim only the algorithmic strength explicitly supported.
